Subject: Pricing for Hosted API pilot (Brightline)

Markus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our engineering team is excited about the latency profile and the KV caching behavior — this looks like what we need for our triage-assist workflows.

Quick ask from procurement: Brightline is committing to a 12-month pilot that we expect will ramp to ~1.7B tokens/month by Q4, with a likely multi-year renewal. Given the scale and the competitive landscape, procurement is asking whether Redwood can provide a 25% off list hosted-API rate for the first 12 months.

We can sign an LOI (attached) to lock the ramp profile and commit to a quarterly business review cadence. If Redwood needs additional commercial protections (usage floors, minimum monthly commitment), we’re open to that.

Can you confirm whether this is possible or whether we should route to an exec approval?

Thanks,
Claire

Subject: Fwd: Pricing for Hosted API pilot (Brightline) — request exec OK for 25%

Ben / Laura — forwarding Brightline's LOI and ask. Key points below: 

- Account: Brightline Health (national telehealth provider)
- Ask: 25% off list hosted-API unit rates for first 12 months
- Expected ramp: 1.7B tokens/month by Q4 (attached forecast)
- Value: multi-year potential, marketplace reference, strategic healthcare vertical win
- Proposed commercial protections: 6-month minimum spend threshold + QBRs + gradual step-down of discount after year 1

I know standard delegated authority covers up to 20% for hosted deals; this is above that. I recommend we approve 25% for the pilot with the following addenda: 1) usage floor equal to 75% of forecast during months 4–12, 2) add SLA credits cap and emergency throttling clause, 3) maintain Redwood standard data handling language.

Attachments: Brightline_LOI_signed.pdf, usage_forecast_Q1-Q4_2027.xlsx, pricing_model_proposal_v3.pptx

Can you weigh in — if you’re comfortable, I’ll loop Mina for formal approval. Need a decision by EOD Wednesday to meet Brightline procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Markus

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pricing for Hosted API pilot (Brightline) — request exec OK for 25%

Hey Markus — thanks for the summary and the pack. Reviewed forecast and model. Quick thoughts: 

- Commercial risk looks reasonable with the LOI and the forecast shape, but we should avoid an open-ended 25% off list without staged guardrails.
- Proposal: Approve 25% off list for months 1–6, then 15% off for months 7–12 unless usage floor (75% of forecast) is met. If they hit >=95% of forecast by month 9, we auto-extend 25% for remaining months.
- Require a 3% implementation credit (one-time) to offset migration/enablement costs and a defined churn clause if they fail to meet floors two quarters in a row.

If you want to keep it simple for procurement, we can present a single-line concession: 25% for 6 months, 15% next 6 months conditional on floors, subject to LOI and DocuSign. That keeps risk contained and gets exec sign-off faster.

Laura — can you bake this into a short amendment and estimate the RevOps impact (ARR dilution) quickly?

Ben
Head of Deal Desk | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Markus / Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. The staged approach is acceptable — Brightline can sign a short amendment that formalizes 25% for months 1–6 and 15% for months 7–12 with the usage floors you described. We prefer no complex clawback language; the team is comfortable with a simple floor-based step-down. 

Two asks from procurement to make this go live this week: 
1) A DocuSign amendment we can sign today
2) Confirmation that technical onboarding support (1 week of dedicated infra time + two runbooks) is included as an implementation credit 

If you can get exec approval for the 25% initial concession, procurement will sign as soon as the amendment hits DocuSign.

Best,
Claire

From: mina_haddad@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2026 17:44:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Fwd: Pricing for Hosted API pilot (Brightline) — exec approval granted (25% initial concession)

Team —

Having reviewed the LOI, the usage forecast, and Ben’s staged-risk proposal, I approve a 25% off list concession for months 1–6 and 15% for months 7–12 subject to the following binding conditions to protect revenue and ops: 

1) Execute the amendment via DocuSign that mirrors Ben's staged plan exactly (25% / 15% conditional on floors).
2) Include a minimum monthly commitment equal to 75% of the ramp forecast for months 4–12.
3) Add an implementation credit line item (one-time) limited to a 3% credit against total first-quarter invoice; technical onboarding resource commitment limited to two engineers for up to 5 days total.
4) Add explicit rollback clause: If usage falls below 50% of forecast for two consecutive months after month 6, Redwood may terminate discount pricing and revert to list; customer will be notified with 30 days cure period.
5) Legal to confirm there are no deviations to Redwood standard data handling and IP clauses; if any legal exceptions are requested, come back to me.

Markus — please send the DocuSign amendment to Claire with the attachments and copy me on the envelope. Laura — estimate ARR impact and track the amendment ID under DL-2026-0839. Ben — please prepare a short one-pager we can use for Sales leadership as a record of this concession.

I’m authorizing this now to keep momentum.

Mina
